pages.title: Abdullah Çatlı
pages.description: Turkish secret government agent, convicted drug trafficker and contract killer.
pages.abstract: Abdullah Çatlı was a Turkish secret government agent, convicted drug trafficker as well as a contract killer for the National Intelligence Organization (MİT). He led the Grey Wolves, the youth branch of the Nationalist Movement Party (MHP), during the 1970s. His death in the Susurluk car crash, while travelling in a car with state officials, revealed the depth of the state's complicity in organized crime in what became known as the Susurluk scandal. He was a hitman for the state, and was involved in the killings of suspected members of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) and the Armenian Secret Army for the Liberation of Armenia (ASALA).

pages.title: Grey Wolves (organization)
pages.abstract: The Grey Wolves, officially known as Idealist Hearths, is a Turkish far-right political movement and the youth wing of the Nationalist Movement Party (MHP). Commonly described as ultranationalist, neo-fascist, Islamo-nationalist, and racist, the Grey Wolves have been described by some scholars, journalists, and governments as a death squad and a terrorist organization. Its members deny its political nature and claim it to be a cultural and educational foundation, citing its full official name, Idealist Hearths Educational and Cultural Foundation.

pages.title: Susurluk car crash
pages.description: 1996 event in Turkey which led to a scandal
pages.abstract: The Susurluk car crash was a car crash that took place on 3 November 1996 in the small town of Susurluk, in Turkey's Balıkesir Province. It resulted in the deaths of three of the passengers: Abdullah Çatlı, a former ultra-rightist militant wanted by police for multiple murders and drug trafficking; Huseyin Kocadağ, a senior police official; and beauty queen and Çatlı's girlfriend Gonca Us. Sedat Bucak, an MP, suffered a broken leg and fractured skull but survived the accident. The Susurluk crash was a key event in the unravelling of the deep state in Turkey. The peculiar associations of the crash victims and their links with Interior Minister Mehmet Ağar led to a number of investigations, including a parliamentary investigation, of what became known as the Susurluk scandal.

pages.title: Ministry of Interior (Turkey)
pages.abstract: The Ministry of Interior or Ministry of the Interior or Interior Ministry is a government ministry of the Republic of Turkey, responsible for interior security affairs in Turkey.

pages.title: Mehmet Ağar
pages.abstract: Mehmet Kemal Ağar is a Turkish former police chief, politician, government minister and leader of the Democratic Party. He was a police officer who rose to General Director of the General Directorate of Security, serving from 1993 to 1995, before entering parliament and serving as a government minister in 1996. Under his reign a close relationship developed between the deep state in Turkey, the Grey Wolves, and the Turkish mafia. It took 15 years until he was tried and sentenced for criminal activities relating to the 1996 Susurluk scandal; he was incarcerated in April 2012 but already released on probation in April 2013.

pages.title: True Path Party
pages.abstract: The True Path Party was a centre-right political party in Turkey, active from 1983 to 2007. For most of its history, the party's central figure was Süleyman Demirel, a former Prime Minister of Turkey who previously led the Justice Party (AP) before it was shut down in the aftermath of the 1980 military coup. The DYP was widely considered the successor of both the AP and the Democrat Party (DP), active in Turkey's early multi-party period.

nytimes_articles.abstract: Advertising column on One Club for Art and Copy's restrospective exhibit, The First 10 Years, devoted to Fallon McElligott's pro-bono campaigns for Children's Defense Fund over last decade; notes that while many agency executives want to do pro-bono work, such accounts make demands on scarce resources, and there is always danger that paying clients may perceive themselves as being given short shift by executives who seem more eager to devote time to pro-bono clients (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Races Ending in Bitterness and Silliness
nytimes_articles.abstract: Last-minute campaigning in Congressional districts in New York, New Jersey and Connecticut turns occasionally vitriolic and zany; map (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Party Leaders Spar, Each Side Predicting Victory on Tuesday
nytimes_articles.abstract: Famous and powerful leaders of both Democratic and Republican parties spend last Sunday of Presidential campaign on television interview programs, predicting victory and commenting on liabilities of voting for opposing candidate; controversy over foreign financing of campaigns seen as major topic (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: The Many Ailments of the Presidents
nytimes_articles.abstract: College of Physicians of Philadelphia exhibition on ailments and injuries suffered by many Presidents while in office raises questions about how much public has ever really known about health of chief executive and about safeguards to monitor Presidential fitness; exhibition organizers hold 25th Amendment, which addresses transfer of power in case of Presidential illness or death, leaves too many questions open to interpretation; photo (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: N.F.L. Concussions Are Not Really Funny
nytimes_articles.abstract: Dave Anderson Sports of The Times column discusses alarmingly high instance of concussions suffered by football players; urges National Football League to conductstudy into matter; photo (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: USA Network To Fallon McElligott
nytimes_articles.abstract: USA Network cable channel names Fallon McElligott to handle its account; billings estimated at $15 million (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Penney Seeks to Purchase Drug Chain for $2.5 Billion
nytimes_articles.abstract: Latest consolidation in drugstore industry is announcement by J C Penney Co that it will acquire Eckerd Corp for $2.5 billion in cash and stock; deal includes assumption of $760 milion in debt, and is one in series of recent acquisitions Penney has made in its Thrift drugstore division; Penney and other drugstore operators are creating regional and national chains so they can cut costs and demand better prices from suppliers; Penney hopes to cut $100 million in that way; Penney and Eckerd say there will be no immediate job cuts but hint that they are possibility in future (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: The Sober Man in the Gray Suit
nytimes_articles.abstract: John Birt, director general of British Broadcasting Corp, has made BBC a more efficient noncommercial broadcaster, but has alienated many employees in the process; his rescue plan has been similar to that adopted by some American networks, including the dismissal of thousands of staff members; Birt sees his primary task as that of turning BBC into efficient noncommercial domestic broadcaster capable of withstanding competition from private British terrestrial channels and satellite-delivered programs; photo; graphs (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: An Old Friend Called Giuliani, and New York's Cable Clash Was On
nytimes_articles.abstract: Court records show that a telephone call to Mayor Rudolph Giuliani from Roger Ailes, former Republican consultant and now chairman of Rupert Murdoch's new 24-hour news channel, was opening maneuver in aggressive campaign by Murdoch's News Corp to gain Giuliani's support in its clash with Time Warner over access to air time on Time Warner's New York cable system; are contained in Time Warner's suit seeking to bar transmission of Fox News Channel on city-operated channel (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Arrested Progress in China
nytimes_articles.abstract: Editorial on need for political reform in China; deplores China's plans to stiffle open political dissent in Hong Kong (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Magazines Learning to Take Not-So-Clueless (and Monied) Teen-Agers More Seriously
nytimes_articles.abstract: Magazines for teen-agers have not changed much in content, but market is changing: teen-agers are rapidly growing segment of population, and they have more of their own money than ever to spend; this excites advertisers, who are now setting aside funds expressly geared toward teen-age market (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: A Balladeer Of Bluegrass Is Now Gone Yet Lives On
nytimes_articles.abstract: Rosine, Ky, home of late Bill Monroe, bluegrass music legend, plans to honor him with theater, monument and museum; Monroe's grave and songs about area attract visitors; map; photos (M)
